title: Detonate the Maximum Bombs
summary: Given a list of bombs, each defined by its coordinates and range, determine the maximum number of bombs that can be detonated by detonating a single bomb.
statement: Given a list of bombs, each defined by its coordinates and range, determine the maximum number of bombs that can be detonated by detonating a single bomb. When a bomb is detonated, it will trigger the detonation of all bombs within its range, which are located within a circular area centered at the bomb's coordinates. Return the total number of bombs that can be detonated under these conditions.
constraints: Each bomb is [x,y,radius]; triggering is directed because radii may differ.
A detonated bomb recursively triggers every center within or on its circular range.
Return the largest cascade size from one starting bomb.
hints: Convert each geometric reach relation into a directed graph edge.
Compare squared distance with squared source radius, then run a reachability search from every bomb.
Add i->j when dx*dx+dy*dy<=r_i*r_i; track the largest visited set.
Graph reachability precisely matches recursive triggering, and trying every possible first bomb finds the maximum cascade.
editorial: Graph reachability precisely matches recursive triggering, and trying every possible first bomb finds the maximum cascade.

tests.explanation: The second bomb reaches the first, so starting at the second detonates both.
Neither center lies in the other range, so the largest cascade has size one.
